topic.title: Dermal papilla-derived BMP4 contributes to epithelial FOXP1-FGF18 signaling in human hair follicle cells
topic.abstract: Bone morphogenetic protein 4 (BMP4) has been implicated in hair follicle telogen maintenance, but its downstream mechanisms in human hair follicle cells remain incompletely understood. We examined whether BMP4 regulates fibroblast growth factor 18 (FGF18) through FOXP1 in dermal papilla-epithelial signaling. In immortalized human dermal papilla cells (iDPCs), cyclosporin A (CsA) decreased BMP4 expression and increased Noggin expression, and the NFAT inhibitor VIVIT produced similar effects. CsA also reduced BMP4 protein levels in culture supernatants. In immortalized human outer root sheath cells (iORSCs), BMP4 increased FGF18 and FOXP1 expression, with significant responses at concentrations as low as 0.1 ng/mL. Noggin and the BMP type I receptor inhibitor LDN193189 suppressed these responses. BMP4 induced Smad1 phosphorylation and increased FOXP1 protein levels, whereas FOXP1 knockdown prevented BMP4-induced FGF18 upregulation. In primary human DPCs, CsA decreased BMP4 expression, and in primary human ORSCs, BMP4 increased FGF18 expression. In Transwell co-culture, CsA pretreatment or BMP4 neutralization attenuated DPC-induced FGF18 and FOXP1 expression, whereas recombinant BMP4 significantly restored their expression. These findings suggest that DPC-derived BMP4 contributes to FOXP1-dependent FGF18 regulation and DPC-epithelial communication relevant to follicular quiescence.
